chunks: ʿAlī, from Muḥammad ibn ʿĪsā, from Yūnus, from Muḥammad ibn Sinān, from al-ʿAlāʾ ibn al-Fuḍayl, from Abī ʿAbdillāh عليه السلام, that he said:
For accidental killing, there is one hundred camels, or one thousand sheep, or ten thousand dirhams, or one thousand dinars.
If it is paid in camels, then it is twenty-five bint makhāḍ, twenty-five bint labūn, twenty-five ḥiqqah, and twenty-five jadhaʿah.

The aggravated blood-money in mistaken killing that resembles intentional killing—where one strikes with a stone or with a stick, one strike or two, not intending to kill him—is in thirds: thirty-three ḥiqqah, thirty-three jadhaʿah, and thirty-four khalifah, all of them covered by the stallion.
If it is sheep, then it is one thousand rams. Intentional killing is subject to retaliation, unless the guardian of the slain is satisfied.

key_terms.الدِّيَةُ الْمُغَلَّظَةُ: the aggravated blood-money due in a form of killing resembling intentional killing
key_terms.الْإِبِلِ: camels, one of the accepted forms of diyah payment
key_terms.الْغَنَمِ: sheep, another accepted form of diyah payment
key_terms.قَتْلِ الْخَطَإِ: accidental killing, for which prescribed blood-money is due
key_terms.وَلِيِّ الْمَقْتُولِ: the legal guardian or heir of the slain person with authority regarding retaliation or acceptance

ai.seo_question: What is the diyah for accidental and quasi-intentional killing in Shia fiqh?
ai.summary: This hadith sets out the legal rulings for blood-money in cases of accidental killing and quasi-intentional killing, specifying the acceptable forms and amounts of compensation. It also distinguishes intentional killing from accidental and شبه العمد cases, stating that intentional killing entails retaliation unless the slain person's guardian accepts otherwise.
